text: v1 of Promises stores everything in browser localStorage only, with no sync, by explicit choice of the owner to keep it simple. The owner wants cross-device sync via a server later. Plan discussed for that step: a Yjs document on the client, the y-websocket provider, and a small self-hosted Hocuspocus server with its SQLite extension, one process serving static files plus WebSocket, access by unguessable list URL. Keep the storage code behind one module so this swap stays contained.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rejected for sync (2026-10): (1) Peer-only WebRTC via y-webrtc: its default public signaling servers are mostly dead. (2) Trystero (WebRTC with Nostr/BitTorrent discovery) plus a custom Yjs adapter: works with no server, but devices only sync while both are open at the same time. (3) Iroh: no browser npm package (needs a custom Rust-to-WASM wrapper crate), and in browsers all traffic goes through n0 relays, whose free public tier is for hobby use only; gossip also needs a known bootstrap peer. The owner chose a real server later instead of any of these.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
